artifacts.summary: Full audit of the 64 agents reachable via a dispatch[] row (research/plan/implement, core + all extensions): derivation method, per-agent .orchestrator-handoff.json mention counts, and the critical finding that 6 of the 8 nonzero-count agents state a prohibition (must be reversed, not appended to) rather than the target obligation.

memory_candidates.content: To enumerate every agent reachable via /orchestrate's dispatch[] row (not aux_dispatch[], not second-level sub-agent delegation), collect the union of routing_agents.{research,plan,implement} and routing_agents_hard.{research,plan,implement} across every agent-system/extensions/*/manifest.json, excluding manifests with routing_exempt:true (literature, slidev) and any non-standard phase keys (e.g. present's 'critique', which is not part of dispatch[]'s fixed {research,plan,implement} phase vocabulary and is invoked by a separate non-orchestrate skill). Second-level sub-agents invoked internally by a router agent (e.g. filetypes-router-agent -> document-agent) never receive orchestrator_mode/handoff_path and are correctly out of scope.

When auditing agent contracts for a missing obligation via grep mention-count of a keyword/filename, a nonzero count can mean the opposite of compliance: in agent-system/extensions/*/agents/*.md, 6 agents (general-implementation-agent, general-research-agent, cslib-implementation-agent, cslib-research-agent, lean-research-agent, lean-research-hard-agent) mention '.orchestrator-handoff.json' only inside explicit MUST-NOT/prohibition/non-writer-by-design language. Treat nonzero mentions as requiring content inspection, not just presence-checking, before assuming an obligation is already stated correctly.
